Set up a local server

OpenCode MCP Server Setup and Troubleshooting

In OpenCode V2, add a local MCP server under mcp.servers in the project config. From the same project, run opencode mcp list and check the server’s status. If it says No MCP servers configured on startup, confirm the config source and check again against the same running OpenCode service before rewriting it.

  1. Add a local MCP server
  2. Choose the next check
  3. The list is empty

  5. Connected, but the tool is missing
  6. See the tested outputs

Add a local MCP server in OpenCode V2

OpenCode starts the command as a subprocess. Use a command you trust and review what it can access. For a minimal check, create an empty project folder, save the sample Node.js server there, and run these commands from that folder with Node.js and OpenCode installed:

opencode --version
node --version
opencode mcp add smoke -- node ./mcp-smoke.mjs
opencode mcp list

The sample serves one tool, healthcheck, which returns the fixed text MCP_OK. It does not read your project files or call an external service. The add command writes a project config entry. To edit an existing config by hand, merge the following structure into it and keep your other settings:

{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "smoke": {
        "type": "local",
        "command": ["node", "./mcp-smoke.mjs"]
      }
    }
  }
}

Use one argument per array entry. A relative script path is resolved from the server process’s working directory. Set cwd when the command needs a particular directory.

What does MCP list show?

See stepsSee stepsSee steps

The list is empty or your server is missing

  1. From the folder where you use OpenCode, run opencode debug config. Check that the output includes the expected configuration file and server entry. Keep the output local if it contains credentials.
  2. For new V2 settings, use mcp.servers.NAME. Check disabled and project or global overrides. V1 uses a server directly under mcp and the inverse enabled field. V2.4.1 loaded our simple V1 entry through compatibility handling. The legacy shape alone did not explain the empty list.
  3. Check opencode mcp list again from the same project against the same service, or open /mcps in your active V2 session. A fresh --standalone invocation starts another private server and can repeat the cold-start result. In our test, the second check showed the server both on the normal background service and on a separately started loopback service.

The OpenCode repository tracks the empty-list startup symptom. If the server still never appears, record the OpenCode version and effective configuration source before changing the connection settings.

The local MCP connection failed

  1. Read the detail after failed. Our missing script returned Connection closed and MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Check the executable in the service’s environment and the script path relative to its configured cwd.
  2. Try the same command and arguments from that working directory. A stdio server can sit quietly while it waits for messages. Immediate exit or a missing-module error points to startup. If it is running, use Ctrl+C to stop the manual check.
  3. Keep ordinary logs on stderr. The MCP stdio transport uses stdout for newline-delimited protocol messages, so a startup banner on stdout can interfere with the handshake.

Remote Streamable HTTP servers use a URL and may require OAuth or headers. Follow OpenCode’s remote server setup for those cases.

The server is connected but a tool is missing

Confirm the server advertises the tool you expect. In our check, OpenCode logged tools=1 after connecting to the sample. The MCP protocol response listed healthcheck. That established discovery. A separate direct request confirmed the sample tool returned MCP_OK.

OpenCode V2 normally groups MCP tools under Code Mode. Check the server namespace and the agent’s permissions before expecting individual tools in a provider’s list. The codemode and permission settings have different roles. Review the OpenCode MCP permission docs and the OpenCode project permission check.

What OpenCode 2.4.1 reported

On macOS, we tested a healthy V2 config, the same config with a missing script, and a simple V1 entry under V2. Each fresh standalone list printed No MCP servers configured. Against a persistent loopback OpenCode service in each test, the next listing showed two successful connections and one explicit startup failure across the three cases. The healthy V2 connection discovered one tool.

Download the configurations, CLI outputs and direct MCP results. We did not run a model turn or test remote authentication. Sources include OpenCode MCP docs, its migration guide and the MCP stdio specification.
